frontier: remove the unbound npm/xterm build path without changing product runtime semantics
observed_anchors: current canonical BOOTSTRAP_MINIMAL and PROGRAM_STATE define ClayVerse as one OCI/Docker-compatible container and EntityOS only as internal substrate
current Dockerfile installed nodejs/npm only to obtain @xterm/xterm@6.0.0 and copied lib/xterm.js plus css/xterm.css
current manifest listed xterm repository hash locking as an open supply-chain gate
npm package metadata identifies @xterm/xterm 6.0.0 with zero dependencies
three independently observed package-lock/pnpm-lock records reproduce the same @xterm/xterm 6.0.0 SHA-512 SRI

mechanism.selected: download the exact registry tarball with Python, verify repository-owned SHA-512 SRI before reading assets, validate archive member paths, copy only the two required regular files atomically, and remove nodejs/npm from the OCI build dependencies
mechanism.simpler_alternative_rejected: keep npm install with only a semantic version pin; this still delegates archive selection/integrity to mutable package-manager metadata at build time
mechanism.structurally_different_alternative_defer: commit the built xterm.js/css bytes directly into the repository; potentially stronger offline provenance but increases repository payload and requires an explicit owner choice about vendored third-party source bytes

counterhypotheses: the helper can accept a digest mismatch due to implementation error
tar metadata can escape the intended vendor directory
the Dockerfile can retain node/npm despite the helper
the observed SRI could be stale or wrong until an exact registry retrieval verifies it
